tb21_profile.skill: Author a .proto service definition, run grpcio-tools/protoc to generate _pb2 and _pb2_grpc stubs, implement the servicer class against them, and serve it on a fixed port as a background process.
tb21_profile.domain: gRPC and Protocol Buffers in Python (grpcio 1.73.0, grpcio-tools), RPC service contracts, code generation, socket servers.
tb21_profile.task_form: Implement-from-spec plus configure-a-service: pinned dependency install, schema authoring, codegen, server implementation, and the server must still be listening when checked.

notes: TMax owns this task: it has a dozen genuine 'implement a Python gRPC microservice' tasks where writing the proto and running protoc is the actual work, which is exactly the TB2.1 skill. Terminal-Lego contributes two real gRPC implementation tasks (task_12106, task_12432) that are as close as anything in TMax and better verified - a place where a new corpus genuinely beats the old pool. CalibForge has no gRPC task, but its protobuf wire-format and protocol-server tasks (RESP2, NATS, JSON-RPC, TCP KV store) are the best-verified 'serve an exact contract on a port' material in the pool. RTS's grpc-server family is 20+ near-duplicates of 'build the Go server, run the client' - the server and proto are given, so transfer is limited and I ranked only a handful. TerminalWorld has one gRPC entry (tw_285202, client side only); SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench have nothing gRPC at all and their entries are filler.
